title: RBACv2 litmus-wave migration and audit holdback stabilization
creator: Ethan Park
description: Goal: perform a staged migration from RBAC v1 to RBAC v2 ensuring no gaps in audit trails, predictable admin controls, and SSO/SAML mapping fidelity. We will validate dual-write, run a reconciliation pipeline, execute litmus waves (small customer cohorts), and keep a final audit holdback wave to verify continuity before global cutover. The emphasis is on observable safety gates, clear rollback hooks, and minimal customer-facing disruption.
acceptance_criteria: Dual-write enabled for all role/assignment APIs with <0.1% error rate in last 72h
Backfill job completes with reconciliation mismatch rate <0.5% and documented fixes for all mismatches
SAML/SSO mapping tests (including multivalued attributes) pass for 3 enterprise fixtures
Audit trail shows 100% continuity (no missing entries) across v1->v2 transition for 30-day window in staging
Runbook and emergency admin bypass validated by oncall during dry-run and added to operations handbook
steps: 1) Enable dual-write for write surfaces (authz-service, admin-console, import jobs) behind feature flag
2) Launch incremental backfill job (shadow-decode reconciliation) to populate authoritative role store from v1 snapshots
3) Run reconciliation pipeline with heuristics and manual triage queue for ambiguous mappings
4) Execute litmus waves: Wave A (internal), Wave B (low-risk customers), Wave C (mid-risk), holdback Wave H (audit holdback customers) to validate end-to-end metrics
5) Validate SSO/SAML mapping using sample IdP configurations and live tenant smoke tests
6) Monitor telemetry (authorization success/fail rates, tail latency, token logs) and audit continuity dashboard during each wave
7) If stability gates pass, schedule rolling cutover and final deprecation of v1 write paths; otherwise execute rollback plan
rollback_plan: Feature-flagged dual-write allows instant fallback by turning off writes to v2 while reads continue from v1. For cutover failures, revert routing using switchboard controller, surface reconciled deltas to customer support, and run an immediate scoped backfill. Emergency admin bypass exposes a temporary elevated bridge role (timeboxed, audited) for platform ops to restore customer access.
comments: 2025-02-12 — Ethan Park: Created ticket and aligned scope with Product and SecEng. Initial approach: staged litmus waves + audit holdback. Requested security review. Added Lina as assignee.

2025-02-14 — Lina Morales: Dual-write feature flag implemented on authz-service (branch: feature/dualwrite-litmus). Smoke tests for basic role create/update pass internally. Observed ~0.3% transient write timeout to v2 under load; investigating backoff tuning.

2025-02-15 — Marcus Patel (Security Review): Reviewed SAML mapping plan. Flagged multivalue attribute case where IdP sends role URIs — added mapping strategy to normalizer and tests. Requested explicit audit event schema versioning (added to acceptance criteria).

2025-02-16 — Lina Morales: Started backfill job in dry-run mode against staging snapshot. Reconciliation discovered 42 mismatches (0.72%) mostly due to legacy 'team' prefix removal. Created manual triage queue and three follow-up fixes (ENG-121322, ENG-121323, ENG-121324).

2025-02-18 — QA: Performed SSO end-to-end test with Okta test tenant. Found SAML assertion timestamp skew that broke our default grace window; increased allowed skew to 120s and added time-skew logging. Ran wave A (internal) canary with 20 internal users — no auth regressions.

2025-02-20 — Lina Morales: Litmus Wave B scheduled for 2025-02-24 (5 low-risk customers). Drafted customer comms and opt-out form. Oncall rotation assigned for wave windows. Next: finalize runbook, finish reconciliation automation, sign security review.

2025-02-20 — Product (Ava Chen): Approved messaging templates for basic and enterprise customers; included rollback notice and contact paths. Requested post-wave retrospective and per-tenant rollback readiness checklist.
